ratings_why.fun: Shop duels and losing on purpose to buy the winner are fresh, but the early game mostly moves stats around and the lone-champion line plays with gaps for several turns before it pays.
ratings_why.distinct: One size-compare verb used on your board, the shop and the enemy is unlike any of today's tribes, and the champion can come from any tribe.

verdict_why: Elder of the Centre loops forever as written and Cantor's text can't be read; both are real fixes.

points.text: Elder of the Centre loops: when the champion gains, it is another friendly unit gaining, so the champion gains again forever. Exclude the champion's own gains.
Cantor's text "Duels your units start happen twice" doesn't parse. Say e.g. "Each duel your units start happens twice", and whether Pilgrim's and Ottokar's chains each count per duel.
Fence-Line Challenger's Start of Turn duel is forced, so from Tier 4 it loses to the shop every turn and shrinks. Let it only duel units it would beat, like Ottokar.
The lone-champion story has no early stage payoff before Prior at Tier 4, so turns 3-6 are weak with gaps. A small Tier 2 'empty slot beside the champion' bonus would start the shape sooner.
Pilgrim plus Keeper plus Cantor takes about three quarters of every shop unit three times a turn; the refresh cap is the right dial, keep the idea hot.

standouts.why: Edge-Strutter lets you lose on purpose and buy the pumped shop unit, a real decision every time.
Grand Master Ottokar eats the small enemies and stops by himself against a tall carry: a capstone with built-in counterplay.
Prior of the Needle Refectory turns empty slots on the zigzag board into a placement puzzle.

weakest.why: Fence-Line Challenger grows early but is forced to lose to the shop later.
Dame Reisig is a plain 1 gold a turn with a trigger that is almost always met.
Dawn Herald hands a quarter of your champion to any bigger enemy, so it backfires in the fights that matter most.

flags.note: Infinite loop: the champion's own permanent gain retriggers Elder of the Centre.
Cantor's rules text can't be read as written.
Pilgrim with Keeper and Cantor can add well past the Tier 6 ceiling each turn.
Ottokar with Keeper and Cantor may decide most fights at Start of Combat against wide boards.
Grit Pit Elder gives permanent stats from in-fight duels too; four a turn caps it, but say whether the fight counts as the turn.
